original_value: At present, a number of users employ an authentication protocol so as to enjoy protected electronic transactions in wireless networks. In order to establish an efficient and robust the transaction system, numerous researches have been conducted relating to authentication protocols. Recently, Kaul and Awasthi presented an user authentication and key agreement scheme, arguing that their scheme is able to resist various types of attacks and preserve diverse security properties. However, this scheme possesses critical vulnerabilities. First, the scheme cannot prevent two kinds of attacks, including off-line password guessing attacks and user impersonation attacks. Second, user anonymity rule cannot be upheld. Third, session key can be compromised by an attacker. Fourth, there is high possibility that the time synchronization trouble occurs. Therefore, we suggest an upgraded version of the user authenticated key agreement method that provides enhanced security. Our security and performance analysis shows that compared, to other associated protocols, our method not only improves the security level but also ensures efficiency.

result.paraphrase: Currently, many users rely on authentication protocols to secure electronic transactions over wireless networks. To build an efficient and robust transaction system, extensive research has been carried out on authentication protocols. Recently, Kaul and Awasthi proposed a user authentication and key agreement scheme, claiming it can withstand various attacks while maintaining multiple security properties. However, the scheme has serious weaknesses. First, it cannot resist two attack types: offline password guessing and user impersonation. Second, it fails to preserve user anonymity. Third, an attacker can compromise the session key. Fourth, there is a strong likelihood of time synchronization problems. Therefore, we propose an improved user-authenticated key agreement method with stronger security. Our security and performance analysis shows that, compared with related protocols, the proposed method not only raises the security level but also remains efficient.
